newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 20.

text.p: Hormone beef decision reversed: The Meat Producers Board has done a U-turn by excluding beef produced with growth hormones from carrying its new quality mark. Page 1.

Ranks closed after 'dog tucker' claim: Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters closed ranks on Monday against Speaker Doug Kidd after his prediction that NZ First would be "dog tucker" at the next election. Page 2.

Henare confident of rivals settling dispute: Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare says he is confident rival groups in Northland can put aside their differences in the interests of settling the Muriwhenua land claim. Page 2.
Colonial Group's spectacular float on the New Zealand and Australian stock exchanges on Monday indicated the huge appetite for new quality local listings, sharebrokers said. Page 13.

Offer tipped to boost Brierley profit for year: Brierley Investments looks on track to book a June-year profit of around $300 million after announcing an unusual public offering that analysts expect will gain the company about $124 million. Page 13.

McCollam boss in for windfall: McCollam Printers chief executive Steve McCollam stands to make at least $4.5 million if a share-swap offer by office products company Blue Star Group is comparable to the cash offer made to other McCollam shareholders. Page 13.

Radio Network ratings drop 'won't affect station revenues': Radio Network is confident of not losing any advertising revenue after a drop in ratings in its Auckland music stations, says Radio Network chief executive Joan Withers. Page 13.

Mills unswayed over Britomart: The Mayor of Auckland, Les Mills, and his council are almost certain to commit more public money to fighting for the besieged Britomart project despite a surprise knockback and damming report on Monday.

Britomart panned but float goes on: Promoters of the Britomart-based Pacific Capital Assets float were visiting financial advisers in Kuala Lampur on Monday when the Auckland Regional Council announced it had declined key resource consents needed for the Britomart project to start.
Skellerup finds a Goldman lifeline: Goldman Sachs' decision to tip more money into Skellerup Group indicates the United States investment bank is not about to walk away from its investment.

Lion scotches brewing rumour: The president market rumour that Lion Breweries is about to start brewing Belgian Stella Artois beer in Auckland is wrong, according to Lion's chief brewer Dr Charles Hahn.
Private heart input may be axed: Health Minister Bill English may issue a directive to end private-sector input to the Christchurch cardiac unit later this week. Page 1.
Saxon merino fibre a 'winner': A North Canterbury firm is beginning to build fibre from the rare saxon merino. Page 27.
Clear losing another manager: Clear Communications' group manager for finance, Michael Braid, has announced his resignation, the company said on Monday. Page 28.
